text:
mike: quick sanity check — profiler traces from last night's long-chat run on p100-pool show heavy slab fragmentation and a cascade of small workspace allocs leading to OOMs. attaching short trace below, can anyone take a look?

sarah: dropping the trace snippet i pulled from the runtime trace. looks like many allocs in 1-8MB range, repeated churn during attention/ffn switch.
```
[2023-11-08T02:14:05Z] slab_alloc: bucket=8MB -> alloc(8,388,608) id=0x7f3c..
[2023-11-08T02:14:05Z] workspace_request: FlashAttn kernel k=64 seq=1024 ws=6,291,456
[2023-11-08T02:14:05Z] workspace_request: Triton FFN ws=7,340,032 fallback=cublaslt_prealloc
[2023-11-08T02:14:06Z] slab_free: id=0x7f3c.. size=8,388,608 -> free_count[8MB]++
[2023-11-08T02:14:07Z] kv_cache_attach: reserve=4,194,304 not_reclaimed
[2023-11-08T02:14:09Z] OOM: workspace alloc failed, tried 8MB, 4MB, fallback->OOM
```

raj: hypothesis: kernel chooser is oscillating between FlashAttn and a Triton FFN variant that uses cublaslt fallback, and the combined allocation patterns leave many partially-used slab pages. Triton kernels currently call cublasLtGetWorkspace with conservative sizes and we sometimes prealloc the max. that interacts badly with our slab fragmentation.

jen: +1. worth checking two levers: 1) reduce initial slab bucket granularity (so a 8MB bucket doesn't get split repeatedly), 2) make cublaslt workspace queries return "just-in-time" sizes rather than preallocating max. we have allocator flags: ALLOC_SLAB_INIT_PCT and SLAB_SPLIT_THRESHOLD.

mike: proposed quick experiment (dev edge only): set ALLOC_SLAB_INIT_PCT=60, SLAB_SPLIT_THRESHOLD=0.6 and disable cublaslt prealloc by setting CUBLASLT_PREALLOC=0. can someone run the bench?

sarah: running now on edge-2 with the env overrides. script: 
```bash
export ALLOC_SLAB_INIT_PCT=60
export SLAB_SPLIT_THRESHOLD=0.6
export CUBLASLT_PREALLOC=0
./scripts/bench_chat.sh --model redwood/open-lite --tokens 500k
```

perf-bot: perf-regression-detector: nightly/long-chat on edge-2: p99 latency baseline(3/8): 145ms -> experiment: 152ms (+4.8%). OOM count baseline=3 -> experiment=0. memory-efficiency score improved by +12%.

raj: those numbers match what i'd expect — small p99 increase for removal of prealloc but OOMs gone. can you also grep for "kv_cache_attach not_reclaimed" and paste a sample? i want to confirm kv buffers are being returned to slab.

sarah: grep output: 
```
[2023-11-08T02:14:07Z] kv_cache_attach: reserve=4,194,304 id=0x12abc not_reclaimed reason=probe_reserve
[2023-11-08T02:14:11Z] slab_reclaim: freed id=0x12abc size=4,194,304 after 3s
```

mike: good that reclaim happened after 3s, but the transient hold combined with many similar buffers causes fragmentation windows. Two action items: (A) add a heuristic to coalesce small KV free events within 5s before returning to slab (batch return), (B) tune kernel chooser to prefer single-path (FlashAttn) for seq>=512 to avoid toggling.

jen: for (A) FYI allocator has a "deferred_free_window_ms" already but default is 0. we can try setting it to 5000ms. i'd PR that as a feature-flag.

raj: for (B) i can add a guard in kernel chooser: if median_seq > 480 and model_type == 'decoder' then prefer FlashAttn unless explicitly flagged. quick change, but need perf regressions on smaller sequences.

mike: thanks. can we also try toggling the cublaslt workspace probing strategy to "query_only" (no prealloc) for a short canary on dedicated? env var: CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_MODE=query_only

sarah: launched canary on dedicated-us-west with query_only + ALLOC flags. early numbers: p99 +6% but throughput stable, no OOMs for last 6h.

perf-bot: perf-alert: dedicated-us-west/canary: token-cost delta -2.3% (wins), p99 delta +3.8%.

mike: ok decision: merge a toggled PR that exposes three knobs: deferred_free_window_ms, ALLOC_SLAB_INIT_PCT, CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_MODE. default keep current values, enable on edge and a dedicated canary for 24h. create a rollback runbook.

jen: i'll own the PR and the rollback runbook. i'll also add a metric for "slab_fragmentation_ratio" and a dashboard tile.

raj: i'll push the kernel chooser guard as a separate PR and add unit tests for seq thresholds. we'll run microbench across seqs 32..2048 to verify no regressions.

sarah: i'll collect traces post-PR and attach a follow-up thread with before/after slab histograms and the kv cache life distribution.

mike: sounds good. follow-ups: jen -> PR + runbook, raj -> chooser PR + benchmarks, sarah -> traces and dashboards. i'll file the support ticket to notify customers of the 24h canary on dedicated. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: assigned perf-bot/alerts to mike,jen for the canary.

mike: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the 24h canary.
